artifacts.summary: Confirms the wrong-premise rationale in git-workflow.md's stash allow-list and the guard's stash_drop-only coverage gap (byte-identity re-confirmed); records verdicts for all 8 scope items (new class name stash_revert, pathspec-scoped push stays permitted, pop/apply stay permitted); flags that please-grant.sh's mint grammar is a second wiring point beyond PG_ACTION_CLASSES that must also be updated to fully reuse the escape hatch.

memory_candidates.content: guard-destructive-git.sh's DESTRUCTIVE_ACTION_CLASS escape hatch (snapshot-marker exemption + pg_grant_consume) generalizes automatically to any new class string set by a detector -- no code change needed in the guard itself beyond the detector. BUT the grant-MINT path (hooks/please-grant.sh) is a second, independent hand-written case/regex grammar that does NOT read from push-grant-lib.sh's PG_ACTION_CLASSES registry, so adding a class to PG_ACTION_CLASSES alone leaves it unmintable via /please. Any future DESTRUCTIVE_ACTION_CLASS addition must update both files, plus please-grant.sh's user-facing accepted-forms error text.

scripts/git-snapshot.sh's default mode internally runs `git stash push -u` as its own snapshot primitive, invisible to guard-destructive-git.sh (subprocess call, never appears as tool_input.command) -- same invisibility pattern as git-commit-scoped.sh. This means the sanctioned snapshot helper carries a narrower version of the same stash-pop-concurrency hazard that direct agent git stash use carries: a later recovery pop from its internal stash could itself be refused under a sibling's intervening write. Known residual risk, not closed by any existing guard mechanism.
